qt: to the Commission Nikolaos Anadiotis (NI) Subject:

The Cooperative Bank of Chania used to offer its clients/shareholders the ‘Chrisi Ependysi’ (Golden Investment) deposit scheme. In 2013 this was replaced with the ‘Apodido’ (My Return on Investment) scheme, in light of the regulatory capital requirements of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013. As many as 300 depositors have complained that the products were presented as safe holdings that could be readily converted to cash and that they were not informed about any changes to the terms and risks1. The Greek administrative authorities remained completely passive towards the bank. By Decisions 520/20262, 944/20263, 1263/2025, 1264/2025, 1219/2025 and 1675/2025, the Greek Supreme Court rejected references to the CJEU for a preliminary ruling, contrary to EU case-law (Case C-627/23), ruling that Directives 2004/39/EC, 93/13/EEC and 2005/29/EC were ‘manifestly’ not applicable to cooperative banks. Affected citizens lodged complaint No 94708/7-8-2026 with the Commission4. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does it consider that offering cooperative bank shares to depositors/consumers is automatically excluded from the scope of the above directives?

Do Articles 28 and 77 of Regulation (EU) 575/2013 allow cooperative shares presented to depositors as ‘readily convertible to cash with a guaranteed return on investment’ to be counted as regulatory capital?
What steps does it intend to take against the Hellenic Republic, so that it complies with its obligations under EU law?
